key_insight: The paper reframes safe adaptation in meta-RL as a reachability problem in information space, where safety depends on both the current state and the agent’s belief about the task.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to build meta-RL agents that can adapt online while explicitly filtering unsafe actions and enforcing safety constraints during learning.
method: Define an information-space safety value function as the probability of avoiding unsafe regions indefinitely.
Show the value function satisfies a self-consistency condition and Bellman equation, enabling learning with meta-RL.
Use the learned safety estimate for safety filtering and constrained policy optimization during adaptation.
evidence_signal: Experiments on meta-RL benchmarks indicate the proposed framework is effective at improving safe adaptation.
watch_item: Safety guarantees depend on the quality of the learned belief-aware safety value function, so performance may degrade if task inference or model approximation is inaccurate.
paper_title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
